title: A 2026 full of land value taxes — Landscape 11
what_was_fetched: One ordinary curl request to the Substack URL (HTTP 200, 267,689 bytes, openly served, saved at fetched/landscape11.html with extracted text in landscape11.txt). Byline Greg Miller (with Daniel Stein, Research Intern, credited at the foot); published 2026-11-25. Primaries fetched (one request per host): revisor.mn.gov HF 161 (200) and nysenate.gov GML 119-r (200). Other linked primaries (lims.dccouncil.gov, njleg.state.nj.us) are already cited by the wiki, so were not fetched. Landscape 11 does not link a Kentucky HB 607 or Virginia HB 282 text; it links CLE's own earlier posts.
verdict: REJECT as a source; use as a map
verdict_reason: Center for Land Economics roundup by its executive director: Tier 2 origin/proponent material under EDITORIAL 4c, never support and never in a lead. Almost every wiki-relevant item is already on a page (HB 282, HB 607/Louisville, NY 119-r, NJ A5386, DC B26-0777, Maryland, ballot measures, ITEP, Kelowna, NZ, Burnham). Only Minnesota HF 161/SF 1422 is a real gap with a fetched Tier 1 primary. The item is not a list of 2026 bills passed; it is largely an election, commentary and media roundup, and it reports no new enactment beyond the three already recorded.
claim_grade: D (advocacy-body roundup; Tier 2). Its factual claims on bills and votes are corroborated only where the wiki already cites Tier 1 texts; the '13 states and DC' tracker figure is a self-description.

events.landscape_claim: Rep. Steve Elkins promises to reintroduce LVT legislation on day one of the January 2027 session; Sen. Omar Fateh is lead author of SF 1422 and Elkins of companion HF 161 (2025 session); Minneapolis mayoral candidates Frey and Fateh both supported a pilot; St. Paul event; Streets.mn explainer.
events.wiki_coverage: Only a passing mention in events/2026-state-lvt-enablement-wave.md (Minnesota listed among stalled 2026 proposals; Fateh named as sponsor, sourced to Landscape Nov 2025). No bill numbers, no Elkins, no dedicated page.
events.primary_fetched: yes, 2026-11-26 (HTTP 200); SF 1422 not fetched (same host, one request per host)
events.primary_confirms: HF 161, 94th Legislature (2025-2026): description 'Cities authorized to create land-value taxation districts'; introduced and referred to Taxes 02/10/2025; eight authors (Elkins first; Gomez, Jones, Smith, Sencer-Mura, Moller, Kraft, Hussein); companion SF1422; the action list ends 04/03/2025 (author added), with no hearing, vote or engrossment recorded. Elkins' reintroduction pledge is not in any primary (source: MinnPost, news).

events.landscape_claim: Nadeau bill would require land valued as if vacant at highest and best use and separate testing of the land component; GGWash and ITEP testimony; CLE's Lars Doucet testified Oct 16.
events.wiki_coverage: Covered in full: events/2026-dc-land-value-assessment-bill.md (introduced 14 July 2026, referral 22 Sept, hearing 16 Oct; cites GGWash, LIMS).
events.gap: No gap. Doucet's Oct 16 testimony and the ITEP testimony appear to be the only uncovered detail; CLE-side testimony is Tier 2 origin material.

events.event: New Jersey A5386 (Brennan; transit value-capture study)
events.landscape_claim: Brennan and Calabrese bill directs EDA to study supplemental transit financing incl. value capture, ground leases; Politico Pro coverage; video.
events.wiki_coverage: Covered in detail: enablement-wave page final section (introduced 10 Sept 2026; cites the NJ Legislature bill text).
events.gap: No gap; wiki is more precise (names no land value tax; not heard in committee).

events.landscape_claim: 'New York extended its authority to fund transit through land value tax'; IBX; Niskanen piece; Landscape 9.
events.wiki_coverage: Covered: enablement-wave page 'New York' section and places/new-york-city.md, plus events/2026-nyc-interborough-express-value-capture.md. Statute itself is not cited as a primary on those pages.
events.gap: Partial gap: the statute text is not cited (BACKLOG only).
events.primary_confirms: GML section 119-r is served; the transit-district subdivision lists value-capture methods including (i) tax increment financing, (ii) a special transportation assessment 'which shall not constitute a tax', (iii) 'land value taxation' defined as allocating an increment of revenue from taxing land at a higher rate than improvements (RPTL s.102(12)), and (iv) combinations. The page carries the note 'Effective until April 1, 2027' for that text. It is the consolidated statute, so it does not show the 2026 budget bill or signing date.

events.event: Other items (YIMBYtown, YIMBY Action primer, Yglesias, Providence PVD Eye, Marohn rerun, Forrester paper, CLE annual report)
events.landscape_claim: Commentary, conferences, op-eds; CLE annual report says three states passed LVT legislation in 2026.
events.wiki_coverage: Forrester covered at research/forrester-lvt-green-growth.md. Others uncovered but all advocacy or commentary (Tier 2/3).

contradictions: Michigan: Landscape says Duggan's LVT 'fell one vote short' at the State House. events/detroit-lvt-proposal.md says HB 4966-4970 (2023) never got a final House floor vote (HB 4966 postponed 11 Oct 2023). A mismatch of characterisation, not of dates; the wiki's primary-sourced account should stand and the Landscape wording should not be used.

Ohio: Landscape says organisers 'did not even get enough signatures' for the property-tax abolition amendment; proposition-13.md says the petition committee suspended its 2026 effort on 5 June 2026 and is aiming at 2027. Not an outright conflict but not equivalent; wiki's wording is the safer one.

No contradiction on state counts: 'three states passed LVT legislation' and 'eight Virginia cities' match the wiki. The '13 states plus DC' figure has no wiki counterpart and counts tracker coverage, not enactments; it must not be paraphrased as thirteen states with LVT law.
No contradiction on the Florida 60% threshold, Oklahoma and Wyoming rejections, Louisville, DC bill, or NJ A5386.
scanner_premise_errors: The scanner calls this a review of 'LVT legislative momentum' in which 'Kentucky and Virginia passed enabling legislation; New York extended LVT transit-funding authority'. The Landscape mentions those only as a one-sentence recap (the NY extension is described as covered in Landscape 9); the body is mostly Minnesota, DC, Virginia local politics, Michigan, NJ, Baltimore, ballot measures, Texas, ITEP, YIMBYtown, commentary and international items.

The scanner says 'prior editions Landscape 8/9 map to the wave page'; true (sources 3 and 5), but Landscape 10 is also cited (source 12, and pittsburgh.md source 6), and the 9 Nov / 17 Nov 2025 editions are cited as well. This is edition 11; no wiki page cites it yet.
The 13-states figure is the tracker's coverage (new laws, bills, emerging efforts, older authority), not a count of states passing LVT laws.
uncertainties: The NYS Senate text of GML 119-r carries 'Effective until April 1, 2027' for the value-capture provision, consistent with the wave page's 'renewed through April 2027'; the 2026 budget bill and signing date were not checked against a primary.

HF 161's record was read on 2026-11-26 and may not show later House action; SF 1422's page was not fetched (same host). Elkins' reintroduction pledge is sourced only to MinnPost (news) and the Landscape.
Whether the NZ Electoral Commission's results confirm TOP's entry to Parliament was not checked; no official link was supplied.
Alexandria's agenda is a draft; wait for an adopted council document before writing it up.

suggested_text.for_gap: Minnesota HF 161 (add to the Minnesota mention on events/2026-state-lvt-enablement-wave.md; cite the revisor.mn.gov bill page as Tier 1 primary)
suggested_text.text: Minnesota's House File 161 of the 2025-26 session, introduced on 10 February 2025 by Representative Steve Elkins and seven co-authors, would authorize cities to create land-value taxation districts. It was referred to the House Taxes Committee, and its legislative record shows no further action after an author was added on 3 April 2025. Its Senate companion is SF 1422.
